description: The gridded EPA US anthropogenic methane inventory publishes estimated methane fluxes for the contiguous United States by source category. The US Environmental Protection Agency and research partners allocate national inventory totals to a 0.1-degree grid. NetCDF annual files cover 2012–2018 in the principal product, and an express extension covers 2012–2020; monthly scaling-factor files are supplied for selected source categories. Categories include natural-gas production, transmission and distribution, petroleum transport, coal mines, landfills and wastewater treatment. Files are openly listed on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0, with a versioned DOI and no fee. The GitHub repository contains the generation code, but its README says selected proprietary source inputs are unavailable publicly. A limitation is that these grids are allocated estimates, not measured leaks at individual facilities. The express extension carries some 2018 spatial patterns forward, so it should not be merged uncritically with principal-product files. This resource can provide emissions context and calibration checks for gas, wastewater and industrial scenarios. The catalogue's data-epa-campd-power-sector-emissions is a distinct EPA emissions source for comparison. No NetCDF file was downloaded.
